questions.question: What is the core delivery invariant in this design?
options: One logical message ID can have independent encrypted delivery state per recipient device
Every recipient device must join the sender's database transaction
A retry always receives a new message ID
The routing service must hold the recipient's content keys
questions.explanation: Stable logical identity prevents duplicate display, while per-device state lets each phone, tablet, web, or desktop session progress independently.

questions.question: What does the playback invariant protect first?
options: Continuous playback within startup, rebuffering, quality, and origin-protection budgets
The maximum possible resolution for every device
A single global catalog database transaction
Training recommendation models during segment download
questions.explanation: A good streaming architecture protects the viewing session and delivery reserve together; a higher rendition is useful only when it remains sustainable.

questions.question: Which state remains authoritative while search, notifications, Actions, and webhooks catch up?
options: The Git object graph and protected references
questions.explanation: Immutable Git objects and the current protected reference define repository history. The other systems are derived consumers that may converge asynchronously.

questions.question: Which statement is the core assignment invariant?
options: Every nearby driver marker is available for assignment
Every trip event must be consumed globally before a driver is assigned
A trip has one authoritative version and at most one assigned driver at a time
The pricing multiplier owns the trip state
questions.explanation: Location, scores, and consumers may be stale or replayed, but only one versioned trip transition can own the driver assignment.
